Theme

Latin word

prōcūrātor

prōcūrātor, prōcūrātōris m.

noun, third declension

an agent, someone who manages affairs for another; governor of a minor province; a manager, the agent who runs things for the owner

In this lexicon

  • agent

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Caecin. 57: aliēnī jūris vicārius; Traupman 169, 219: itinerum prōcūrātor, travel agent

  • governor

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. prōcūrātor: of the governors of small provinces under the emperors; Traupman 179; Traupman 323

  • manager

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.249; Cic. Caecin. 57: prōcūrātor, aliēnī jūris vicārius (Lewis & Short); Traupman 318; Traupman 388

  • itinerum prōcūrātor: travel agent

    modern

Examples

  • is quī lēgitimē prōcūrātor dīcitur, omnium rērum ejus quī in Ītaliā nōn sit absitve reī pūblicae causā quasi quīdam paene dominus, hoc est aliēnī jūris vicārius

    the man who is properly called an agent: for someone who is not in Italy, or is away on public business, he is almost a kind of owner of everything, that is, a deputy for another’s rightsCic. Caecin. 57

    In the entry for agent

  • vīlicum vocet, roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet

    let him call in his manager and ask what work has been done and what remainsCato Agr. 2.1

    In the entry for manager

  • sī mandandum aliquid prōcūrātōrī … aut imperandum vīlicō est

    if some instruction has to be given to the manager … or an order to the foremanCic. de Or. 1.249

    In the entry for manager
